title: a taken ticket clears its own unqueued trouble
intention: A ticket that queues at a gate and is taken clears its own standing ticket-unqueued-<id>-at-<gate> trouble; a ticket with no standing raise sends no clear.
why: Measured 2026-11-11: ticket-unqueued-91a27edfdd81-at-clearance stood at 3x and -at-design at 2x after 91a27edfdd81 crossed PROVED through clearance; Ticket.queue (cairn/machines/ticket/ticket.py:190) raises on a refusal and nothing clears on the later success. CC cleared four by hand through ModuleRaiser('ticket').
traces_to: Law 7; outline 3.3.4.3 (a ticket queues itself at a gate and raises when no handler takes it).
how: Ticket.queue: when queued and its own trail's newest record naming ticket-unqueued-<id>-at-<gate> is a raise, clear_trouble it (by the ticket id, what_changed 'queued at <gate>: the gate took it'). A red-first proof over a scratch roots table.

clauses.claim: a ticket refused at clearance and then taken at clearance leaves its trail's newest record naming ticket-unqueued-<id>-at-clearance a clear_trouble
a ticket taken at clearance with no prior raise writes no clear_trouble record

decisions.text: D1: Ticket._stands_raised(identity) reads self.diagnostic_trail(): the newest *.raise_trouble.json / *.clear_trouble.json (names sorted descending) whose pointer is identity decides; none is False. Ticket.queue, when queued, clears the gate's unqueued identity if it stands raised.
D2: the red-first proof, one tooth per clause, Ticket(plan, roots=scratch) with a scripted participant (refuse then accept); the house runner.
